title: Absolute-series domination and bounded nonnegative subsums
statement: Let $I$ be any set and let $K=\mathbf R$ or $\mathbf C$, with its usual absolute value [def-weil-complex-absolute-value] (restricted to $\mathbf R$ when appropriate). Summability means convergence of the net of finite subsums. If $u:I\to K$ and $v:I\to\mathbf R_{\geq0}$ satisfy $|u_i|\leq v_i$ and $\sum_i v_i=V<\infty$, then both $(|u_i|)_i$ and $(u_i)_i$ are summable and $|\sum_i u_i|\leq V$. Also, if $w:I\to\mathbf R_{\geq0}$ and $B\in\mathbf R$ satisfy $\sum_{i\in F}w_i\leq B$ for every finite subset $F\subset I$, then $w$ is summable and $\sum_i w_i\leq B$.
